Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT

    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-33017", "CVE-2026-21858", "CVE-2025-68613", "CVE-2026-3055", "CVE-2026-39987", "CVE-2026-34486", "CVE-2026-33824")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-33017", "CVE-2026-21858", "CVE-2025-68613", "CVE-2026-3055", "CVE-2026-39987", "CVE-2026-34486", "CVE-2026-33824")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId

| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High

ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:

            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

Aikido
2026-07-29 7 use cases 2 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Recon, stolen credentials, hidden C2, and rebuild-or-patch. Four Hugging Face breach decisions that show whether you can catch an attack in progress. Category: News

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Recon tool reading K8s service-account token or /proc/self/environ inside a container
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Cloud instance metadata (IMDS 169.254.169.254) queried by a recon tool inside a workload · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Recon tool reading K8s service-account token or /proc/self/environ inside a container AIReconnaissance Medium
Hunts an interactive/recon binary (cat, curl, python, base64, xxd) reading the mounted Kubernetes service-account token path or /proc/self/environ inside a workload — the day-1 in-pod enumeration the article describes ('a pod reading /proc/self/environ, inspecting service-account tokens'). Distinguishes credential/environment harvesting from a normal application startup read. Rationale: Uses the article's literal strings '/proc/self/environ' and 'service-account tokens' (mounted at /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount) plus recon-tool binaries, so it fires on enumeration rather than a library's normal token read. Cross-checked the K8s SA-token-theft chain in Unit42 and TheHackerNews' breach coverage. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/openai-agent-used-exposed-credentials.html • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/modern-kubernetes-threats/ • https://aquilax.ai/blog/kubernetes-service-account-token-theft
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1613 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Init container or entrypoint script that cats the SA token for debugging
  • CI/CD job (e.g. Helm, kubectl-in-pod) echoing token path during setup
  • Observability agent reading /proc/<pid>/environ for process metadata enrichment
  • Developer running an interactive shell in a pod during troubleshooting
  • Security scanner/CIS-benchmark tool auditing token mounts
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("kubelet","containerd","dockerd") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("entrypoint","docker-entrypoint","helm"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the pod/node (DeviceName), the process lineage, and whether the reader is the workload's own app or an injected shell/tool; pull the full command line and parent. 2) Contain: if the reader is not the expected app, cordon the node, kill the pod, and rotate the pod's service-account token and any secrets it could reach. 3) Hunt: pivot on the same DeviceName for subsequent connections to 169.254.169.254 (IMDS), privileged pod creation in K8s audit, and outbound to pastebin/request-capture/file-sharing services indicating C2 staging.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName in~ ("cat","head","tail","curl","wget","python","python3","sh","bash","dash","busybox","base64","xxd","strings")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount","/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount","/proc/self/environ")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("cat","head","tail","curl","wget","python","python3","sh","bash","busybox","base64","xxd","strings")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount","/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount","/proc/self/environ")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cloud instance metadata (IMDS 169.254.169.254) queried by a recon tool inside a workload AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts a container-side recon binary (curl, wget, python, busybox) connecting to the cloud metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254 / 169.254.170.2) — the article's 'queried cloud metadata' step used to harvest node IAM credentials. Filtering on the recon tool separates credential theft from legitimate cloud-SDK IMDS calls. Rationale: Anchors on the well-known IMDS IPs (169.254.169.254 for AWS/Azure/GCP, 169.254.170.2 for ECS) paired with recon binaries, matching the article's 'queried cloud metadata' credential-harvest step while excluding in-app SDK IMDS traffic. IMDS-to-IAM abuse corroborated by Unit42/SecureByDezign. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/modern-kubernetes-threats/ • https://www.securebydezign.com/articles/kubernetes-pod-escape-cloud-takeover.html
ATT&CKT1552.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • cloud-init / bootstrap scripts curling IMDS for instance identity or user-data
  • kube2iam / kiam / IRDS sidecars that proxy IMDS via curl-like helpers
  • Health-check scripts querying instance-id or region from metadata
  • aws-cli/gcloud shell wrappers invoked by legitimate automation
  • Debugging session where an engineer manually curls IMDS
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("cloud-init","user-data","kube2iam","instance-id","api-token"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the initiating process command line — did it hit the credentials path (/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ or /computeMetadata/v1/) and was IMDSv2 token flow used? Identify the host/pod and its IAM role. 2) Contain: revoke/rotate the node or pod IAM role credentials, and add a GuardDuty/SCP guardrail; if creds were retrieved, assume they are compromised and rotate. 3) Hunt: pivot to CloudTrail for AssumeRole/API calls made with those temporary credentials from a source IP outside the VPC (see UC4), and check for privileged pod creation on the same node.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteIP in ("169.254.169.254","169.254.170.2")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("curl","wget","python","python3","sh","bash","busybox","perl","ruby","nc","ncat")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("169.254.169.254","169.254.170.2")
| where NetworkDirection == "Outbound" or isempty(NetworkDirection)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, Url
| order by TimeGenerated desc

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

Logging-operator Flow/Output CRD injects Fluentd @type exec block (CVE-2026-54680) AIDelivery High
Hunts creation/modification of logging.banzaicloud.io Flow/Output/ClusterFlow/ClusterOutput resources whose record_transformer.records value carries injected Fluentd config — block-close tags (</record>, </filter>), a new <match **> block, or an @type exec directive. This is the exact CVE-2026-54680 injection vector at the Kubernetes API layer, before the malicious config is ever rendered to fluent.conf. Rationale: Uses the exact CVE-2026-54680 vector: record_transformer.records value carrying </record>/</filter>/<match **>/@type exec inside a logging.banzaicloud.io Flow/Output CRD. Kubernetes audit RequestObject captures the raw injected payload before rendering. Corroborated by GitLab GLAD and cvereports. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/kube-logging/logging-operator/CVE-2026-54680/ • https://cvereports.com/reports/CVE-2026-54680
ATT&CKT1190 T1609
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Flow using record_transformer with an XML/HTML-like string value that happens to contain angle-bracket tags
  • A security team deploying a benign PoC/test Flow in a lab namespace to validate the patch
  • Operators migrating configs that legitimately reference an out_exec pipeline (rare but possible)
  • GitOps controller (ArgoCD/Flux) re-applying a stored Flow manifest, causing repeated update events
Suppression filter
| where Payload has_any ("@type exec","<match **>") // require the exec/match directive, not just any angle bracket, to drop benign XML-in-value FPs
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full RequestObject from the audit event and confirm record_transformer.records contains a block-close (</record>) followed by <match **> and @type exec — that structure is not legitimate config. Identify the User.username and source namespace. 2) Contain: delete the malicious Flow/Output, cordon the affected tenant namespace's ability to create logging CRDs (RBAC), and restart/inspect the Fluentd aggregator pod for the rendered fluent.conf and any dropped files (e.g. /tmp/pwned). 3) Hunt: pivot to UC on fluentd process spawning shells and IMDS access from the aggregator pod within the same window; review all Flow/Output creates by that principal over 30d.
AKSAudit
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Verb in ("create","update","patch")
| where RequestUri has "logging.banzaicloud.io"
| where RequestUri has_any ("flows","outputs","clusterflows","clusteroutputs")
| extend Payload = tostring(RequestObject)
| where Payload has "record_transformer"
| where Payload has_any ("@type exec","</record>","</filter>","<match **>")
| project TimeGenerated, User=tostring(User.username), Verb, RequestUri, ResponseStatus=tostring(ResponseStatus.code), Payload
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Fluentd aggregator pod spawns shell/curl via injected out_exec (CVE-2026-54680 RCE) AIExploitation High
Detects the Fluentd aggregator (ruby/fluentd process) spawning /bin/sh, curl, wget or id — the observable result of Fluentd's core @type exec plugin flushing an injected <match> buffer and running attacker commands. Directly matches the article PoC ('/bin/sh -c "id > /tmp/pwned"'). Rationale: Fluentd out_exec spawns '/bin/sh -c "<command>"' from the ruby aggregator process — the article's PoC command chain. Parent=fluentd/ruby + child=shell/curl is a combination Fluentd never legitimately produces, making it high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://docs.fluentd.org/output/exec • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/kube-logging/logging-operator/CVE-2026-54680/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1609
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A custom-built Fluentd image that legitimately uses an exec_filter/out_exec pipeline for enrichment (rare, config-visible)
  • Container liveness/exec health probes running sh inside the fluentd pod via kubelet (parent would be runc/containerd, not fluentd — usually excluded)
  • Debugging: an operator kubectl-execs into the fluentd pod and runs sh (parent is containerd-shim, not fluentd)
  • Fluentd plugin that shells out to gzip/logrotate during buffer rotation
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("liveness","readiness","healthz") ) // drop probe-driven shells
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the full child ProcessCommandLine — if it contains /bin/sh -c with curl to 169.254.169.254, id, or writes to /tmp, treat as confirmed RCE. Confirm the parent is the fluentd aggregator PID. 2) Contain: kill the aggregator pod, snapshot it for forensics, rotate any IAM/instance credentials the node role holds, and freeze logging-CRD create RBAC for tenant namespaces. 3) Hunt: correlate back to the Flow/Output CRD create (UC 1) that seeded the injection and forward to IMDS/lateral-egress UCs for the same pod within the window.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("fluentd","ruby") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "fluentd"
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","curl","wget","id","nc","ncat")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("fluentd","ruby") or ParentProcessCommandLine has "fluentd"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","curl","wget","id","nc","ncat")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Fluentd process spawns shell via out_exec plugin

Fluentd aggregator pod reaches EKS Instance Metadata Service (169.254.169.254) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects a Fluentd aggregator pod (or a shell/curl child spawned by it) connecting to the link-local IMDS endpoint 169.254.169.254 — the article's confirmed post-RCE step for stealing node/instance role credentials on EKS. Restricted to shell/curl/wget initiators to separate the injected command path from legitimate ruby-SDK IMDS use. Rationale: 169.254.169.254 IMDS access by a shell/curl child (not the ruby SDK) is the article's confirmed EKS 1.35 credential-reach step. Scoping the initiator to sh/curl/wget separates the injected out_exec command from legitimate ruby-based instance-profile use. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/kube-logging/logging-operator/CVE-2026-54680/
ATT&CKT1552.005 T1580
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Fluentd S3/CloudWatch output plugin fetching instance-profile creds via the ruby AWS SDK (ruby initiator — excluded by the shell filter)
  • A sidecar or node agent using curl against IMDS for legitimate metadata (different pod/process — check pod identity)
  • kube2iam/IRSA proxy intercepting IMDS calls on some nodes
  • Cluster bootstrap scripts querying IMDS during node join (transient, node-boot window)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ruby") // ruby AWS SDK IMDS use is legitimate
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the initiating process is a shell/curl child of fluentd and the command targets /latest/meta-data or /latest/api/token — that is credential theft, not SDK use. Capture the node's instance-profile role ARN. 2) Contain: revoke/rotate the node role's temporary credentials, apply IMDSv2 hop-limit=1 and require tokens, and cordon/drain the node. Kill the fluentd pod. 3) Hunt: pull CloudTrail for the stolen role ARN for anomalous AssumeRole/API use off-node, and check for lateral egress from the same pod (next UC).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP == "169.254.169.254"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","curl","wget","nc","ncat")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName has_any ("fluentd","ruby") or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("sh","bash")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr == "169.254.169.254"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol, Url, DvcAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Unexpected write to Fluentd fluent.conf introducing exec/block-close directives AIInstallation Medium
Hunts file-write activity against the rendered Fluentd config (fluent.conf under /fluentd/etc or /etc/fluent) inside aggregator pods, and — where content is captured (auditd/AMSI-equivalent script scan) — flags introduction of @type exec or </record>/</filter> block-close tags. Catches the CVE-2026-54680 injection at the point the operator writes the poisoned config to disk. Rationale: Article states injected CRD strings are written 'directly into fluent.conf without escaping'; the rendered config path (/fluentd/etc/fluent.conf) is the on-disk artifact. File-event telemetry gives metadata (writer process) even where content isn't captured, so this is a supporting hunt pivot rather than a content match. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mjqf-28ph-426h
ATT&CKT1565.001 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate logging-operator reconcile writing an updated fluent.conf after a benign Flow/Output change
  • Fluentd config-reload sidecar (e.g. configmap-reload) rewriting the mounted config
  • Helm/operator upgrade re-rendering the aggregator config
  • Node reboot / pod reschedule re-mounting the config Secret (may appear as a write)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("kubelet","containerd","runc","configmap-reload") // exclude mount/reload writers
Response runbook
1) Triage: for each write, base64-decode the current fluentd.conf Secret (<logging>-fluentd-app) and grep for '@type exec' / injected <match **> — presence confirms a poisoned render. Note the writing process/account. 2) Contain: roll the aggregator back to the last known-good config, delete the offending Flow/Output CRD, and restart the pod. 3) Hunt: correlate to the CRD-create UC (same principal/namespace) and to fluentd shell-spawn / IMDS UCs to confirm whether the injected exec block already fired.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName == "fluent.conf"
| where FolderPath has_any ("/fluentd/etc","/etc/fluent")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("kubelet","containerd","runc")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFileName == "fluent.conf"
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/fluentd/etc","/etc/fluent")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername, EventType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Write to Fluentd fluent.conf by unexpected process

Fluentd RCE pod fans out to internal cluster ranges (post-exploitation lateral movement) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects a shell/curl/nc/python child of the Fluentd aggregator making a burst of connections to RFC1918 cluster ranges (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16) — internal service discovery / port-scanning from a compromised aggregator pod after CVE-2026-54680 RCE. Threshold on distinct ports/hosts within a short window separates scanning from normal log routing. Rationale: Article confirms the Fluentd pod has cluster/network reach (used for IMDS). Post-RCE, a shell/curl/nc child of fluentd hitting many distinct internal ports/hosts is service discovery. Parent=fluentd + private-range fan-out + port-count threshold is the discriminator from benign single-destination log routing. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mjqf-28ph-426h
ATT&CKT1046 T1021
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Fluentd legitimately forwarding to multiple internal Output endpoints/Elasticsearch/Loki nodes (ruby initiator — excluded by shell filter)
  • A service-mesh sidecar (Envoy/Istio) proxying many internal connections on the same pod IP
  • Cluster monitoring agent (Prometheus node-exporter scrape targets) sharing the node
  • CI/debug tooling temporarily run inside the namespace performing health checks
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ruby") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("envoy","pilot-agent") // exclude SDK routing and mesh sidecars
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the initiating process is a non-ruby shell/tool child of fluentd and the destinations are sequential ports or many cluster service IPs — that pattern is discovery, not routing. 2) Contain: apply a NetworkPolicy denying egress from the fluentd pod except its declared Output sinks, kill the pod, and review kube-audit for any subsequent access to secrets/serviceaccount tokens. 3) Hunt: enumerate which internal services responded, check those services for follow-on auth attempts from the pod IP, and tie back to the seeding Flow CRD and IMDS credential theft UCs.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","python3")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName has_any ("fluentd","ruby") or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("sh","bash")
| where ipv4_is_private(RemoteIP)
| summarize DistinctPorts=dcount(RemotePort), DistinctHosts=dcount(RemoteIP), SamplePorts=make_set(RemotePort, 20), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where DistinctPorts > 15 or DistinctHosts > 15  // burst = scanning, not normal log routing
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr)
| summarize DistinctPorts=dcount(DstPortNumber), DistinctHosts=dcount(DstIpAddr), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated) by SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where DistinctPorts > 15 or DistinctHosts > 15  // host-scoped burst; confirm src is the fluentd pod/node
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.name:(nmap OR nc OR ncat) @process.command_line:(*10.* OR *172.* OR *192.168.*)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ContextImageFileName=/\/(sh|bash|dash|curl|wget|nc|ncat|python3?)$/i
| cidr("10.0.0.0/8", field=RemoteAddressIP4) OR cidr("172.16.0.0/12", field=RemoteAddressIP4) OR cidr("192.168.0.0/16", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName], function=count(field=RemotePort, distinct=true))
| _count > 15

Prebid-server SSRF payload in OpenRTB2 auction request parameters AIExploitation Low
Hunts inbound requests to prebid-server's /openrtb2/ endpoints carrying bidder-adapter host/subdomain parameters that resolve to internal, loopback, link-local or cloud-metadata destinations. This targets CVE-2026-54735 at the parameter layer — catching the crafted host value before it triggers an outbound forged request. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact mechanism — bidder parameters interpolated into outbound URLs — plus prebid's documented /openrtb2/ endpoints and the canonical SSRF targets (169.254.169.254 metadata IP, RFC1918, loopback). Confidence is Low/FP high because most adapter params ride in the POST JSON body, so this fires cleanly only where the WAF/app tier logs request bodies or GET-style params. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4p3g-4hcj-wpvx • https://cve.threatint.com/CVE/CVE-2026-54735 • https://docs.prebid.org/prebid-server/endpoints/openrtb2/pbs-endpoint-auction.html • https://docs.prebid.org/dev-docs/pbs-bidders.html
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate bidder params that embed geo/region tokens resembling private IP octets (e.g. '10' region codes)
  • Internal QA/load testing pointing an adapter at a staging endpoint on a private IP
  • Security scanners (Burp/Nessus) probing /openrtb2/ with SSRF payloads during an authorized test
  • Load-balancer or uptime monitors hitting /openrtb2/ health probes
  • CDN/WAF appending internal origin hostnames into the logged URL
Suppression filter
| where not(RequestClientApplication has_any ("Nessus","Burp","Nuclei","zgrab")) and SourceIP !startswith "10."
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full request body/URL and identify which bidder adapter param carried the internal/metadata host; confirm the source IP is external and not a known scanner/QA range. 2) Contain: if prebid-server < v4.4.0, disable the abused dynamic-hostname adapter (article workaround) and block the source IP at the WAF; prioritize patching to v4.4.0. 3) Hunt: correlate the request timestamp with UC 'Outbound anomaly' and 'Metadata theft' hunts on the same prebid host to confirm whether a forged outbound request actually fired.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL has "/openrtb2/"
| where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)(169\.254\.169\.254|169\.254\.170\.2|metadata\.google\.internal|127\.0\.0\.1|localhost|0\.0\.0\.0|10\.[0-9]|192\.168\.|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.)"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Prebid-server outbound requests to internal ranges / internal host fan-out (SSRF) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the prebid-server process making outbound connections into RFC1918 / link-local space, and in particular fanning out to many distinct internal hosts within a short window — the observable server-side effect of CVE-2026-54735 being used to reach internal services or scan the network. Rationale: The article's core impact is 'HTTP requests to unintended destinations ... exposing internal network services.' Rather than an allowlist of bad ranges, this baselines the prebid-server process's normal peers and alerts on previously-unseen internal peers plus a fan-out threshold — the network shape of SSRF-driven internal reach/scanning. Anchored to the concrete process name 'prebid-server'. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4p3g-4hcj-wpvx • https://docs.prebid.org/dev-docs/pbs-bidders.html
ATT&CKT1046 T1190
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • prebid-server legitimately calling internal Prebid Cache / analytics services over private IPs
  • East-west container-to-container traffic in a Kubernetes/service-mesh deployment inflating distinct-dest counts
  • Internal ad-exchange peering reached over a private interconnect
  • Monitoring/health-check agents co-located with the origin host
  • Blue/green or autoscaling events where new internal cache endpoints appear and trip the baseline anti-join
Suppression filter
| where not(Dests has_any ("prebidcache"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: review the destinations — are they known Prebid Cache/analytics hosts or unexpected infra (DBs, admin consoles, hypervisor mgmt)? Check the port spread (scan-like sequential ports vs one service port). 2) Contain: isolate/patch the prebid host to v4.4.0 and add an egress policy limiting prebid-server to approved bidder/cache CIDRs. 3) Hunt: pivot to the metadata-theft UC on the same host and to inbound /openrtb2/ requests immediately preceding the outbound burst to identify the triggering bid request.
let Baseline = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp between (ago(30d) .. ago(1d))
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "prebid-server"
    | where RemoteIPType == "Private"
    | summarize by RemoteIP;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "prebid-server"
| where RemoteIPType == "Private"
| join kind=leftanti Baseline on RemoteIP
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), DistinctInternalDests=dcount(RemoteIP), Ports=make_set(RemotePort,20), Dests=make_set(RemoteIP,50) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName
| where DistinctInternalDests >= 5   // 5 previously-unseen internal peers in 24h = SSRF-driven reach/scan
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where NetworkDirection == "Outbound"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) or DstIpAddr startswith "169.254."
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), DistinctInternalDests=dcount(DstIpAddr), Ports=make_set(DstPortNumber,20), Dests=make_set(DstIpAddr,50) by SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where DistinctInternalDests >= 10   // internal host fan-out from a single origin in 10m = scan-like
| order by FirstSeen desc

Prebid-server access to cloud metadata service (169.254.169.254) via SSRF AIActions on Objectives Medium
High-fidelity alert on the prebid-server process connecting to the cloud instance metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254 / 169.254.170.2), and a companion CloudTrail hunt for instance-role credentials being used from off-instance IPs — the credential-theft path implied by 'host environment data extraction' in CVE-2026-54735. Rationale: The article title/body call out 'host environment data extraction'; the canonical realization of SSRF on a cloud host is a request to 169.254.169.254 to steal the instance role. Scoping to InitiatingProcessFileName == 'prebid-server' makes the endpoint side high-fidelity, and the CloudTrail companion catches the stolen role token being replayed from an external IP. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4p3g-4hcj-wpvx • https://cve.threatint.com/CVE/CVE-2026-54735 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/005/
ATT&CKT1552.005
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • prebid-server using the AWS/GCP SDK default credential chain, which legitimately queries IMDS at startup for region/role
  • IMDSv2 token fetch (PUT /latest/api/token) issued by an embedded SDK during normal operation
  • Sidecar/agent frameworks bundled in the container image reading instance identity
  • Autoscaling re-launch causing a burst of legitimate first-start IMDS calls
  • CloudTrail AssumedRole calls from a NAT-gateway public IP misclassified as off-instance
Suppression filter
| where RemotePort != 80 or InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--aws-region"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm whether the IMDS hit correlates with process startup (often legit SDK) or with runtime bid traffic (suspicious); capture the InitiatingProcessCommandLine and any preceding inbound /openrtb2/ request. 2) Contain: if unexpected, revoke/rotate the instance role credentials immediately, enforce IMDSv2 with hop-limit 1, and patch to v4.4.0. 3) Hunt: run the CloudTrail companion for the instance role's session issuer used from external IPs, and review STS AssumeRole/GetSessionToken and any new IAM/S3 actions in the following hour.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "prebid-server"
| where RemoteIP in ("169.254.169.254", "169.254.170.2")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("169.254.169.254", "169.254.170.2")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol, DvcHostname
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Prebid-server SSRF filter-bypass via encoded internal host in request AIExploitation Low
Hunts /openrtb2/ requests whose parameters use URL/double-URL/hex/decimal-IP encoding to smuggle an internal or metadata host past naive input filters — the obfuscated variant of the CVE-2026-54735 SSRF payload. Rationale: The advisory notes the flaw is 'without proper input validation' and the v4.4.0 fix prohibits certain hostname characters — implying attackers will encode payloads to slip past filters. Patterns target the well-known SSRF encodings for 169.254.169.254/127.0.0.1 (double-encoding %25, encoded octets %31%36%39, decimal 2852039166, octal 017700000001, hex 0x). Low confidence because it depends on request-body/query logging and encoded strings are inherently noisy. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4p3g-4hcj-wpvx • https://cve.threatint.com/CVE/CVE-2026-54735
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimately URL-encoded creative/macro parameters in bid requests
  • Analytics/tracking URLs passed as encoded params by adapters
  • Double-encoding introduced by an upstream CDN or proxy normalization
  • Base64 creative blobs that coincidentally contain '0x' or long hex runs
  • Automated scanners fuzzing the endpoint with encoded payloads during authorized testing
Suppression filter
| where not(RequestClientApplication has_any ("Nessus","Burp","Nuclei","zgrab"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: URL-decode the flagged parameter (one or two passes) and determine the final host it resolves to — internal/metadata means true positive. 2) Contain: block the source IP at the WAF, disable the abused dynamic-hostname adapter, and patch to v4.4.0 (which strips disallowed hostname characters). 3) Hunt: check the same source IP for the plaintext SSRF UC and pivot to the prebid host's outbound/metadata UCs to see if any encoded attempt succeeded in firing a forged request.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL has "/openrtb2/"
| where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)(%25[0-9a-f]{2}|%32%35%34|%31%36%39|%6d%65%74%61|0x[0-9a-f]{6,}|2852039166|017700000001|127%2e0%2e0%2e1|169%2e254)"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79") or SHA1 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79") or MD5 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79") or SHA1 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79") or MD5 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

@hypequery/clickhouse SQLi: backslash-quote / JSON-apostrophe payload at web edge (CVE-2026-54658) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts inbound HTTP requests carrying the two CVE-2026-54658 injection signatures against apps backed by @hypequery/clickhouse: a parameter value ending in a backslash immediately before a quote (vector 1, the ClickHouse C-style escape) and an apostrophe breaking out of a JSON-serialised object/array param (vector 2). The trailing backslash-before-quote (`\'` / `%5C%27`) is the distinctive artifact that separates this from generic `' OR 1=1` SQLi. Rationale: Uses the article's exact vector-1 artifact (trailing backslash escaping the closing quote, `x\` -> `\'`) and the `' OR 1=1 --` breakout common to both vectors; the backslash-before-quote is ClickHouse-specific and rare in benign traffic, giving higher fidelity than a plain OR-1=1 signature. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6wcc-39rp-hh9p • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-54658 • https://cve.threatint.com/CVE/CVE-2026-54658
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Apps that accept Windows paths (e.g. `C:\dir\`) followed by quoted values in query strings
  • Security scanners / pentest tooling (Burp, sqlmap) running authorised assessments
  • Regex or LIKE patterns submitted by users that legitimately contain `\'`
  • URL-encoded JSON bodies with escaped quotes in normal API traffic
  • Analytics/BI front-ends that pass raw filter expressions containing `--` as a literal dash
Suppression filter
| where not (csUriStem has_any ("/health","/static/","/assets/") or csUserAgent has_any ("sqlmap","burp") and cIP in ("<authorised-scanner-ips>"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full request (URI + body) and confirm the backslash-quote or JSON-apostrophe lands inside a parameter routed to a ClickHouse query; check the source IP's request history for enumeration bursts. 2) Contain: block the source IP at the WAF, and confirm the app's @hypequery/clickhouse version — if <2.5.1, prioritise upgrade to 2.5.1 (2.0.2 fixes only vector 1). 3) Hunt: pivot to ClickHouse query_log for the same time window to see whether the injected `OR 1=1 --` or broken JSON literal actually executed (see companion query_log UC).
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| extend Q = tolower(strcat(csUriQuery, " ", csUriStem))
| where Q matches regex @"%5c%27" or Q matches regex @"\\'"
    or (Q has "%27" and (Q has_any ("or%201=1","or 1=1") or Q has_any ("%2d%2d"," --")))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, scStatus, csUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable @hypequery/clickhouse package (<2.5.1) present in node_modules AIReconnaissance High
Exposure hunt for hosts carrying a vulnerable @hypequery/clickhouse install. Surfaces the package directory and its files so an analyst can confirm the version against the CVE-2026-54658 fix line (2.0.2 closes vector 1; 2.5.1 closes vector 2 and is the only fully-patched release). Pairs with the web-edge and query_log UCs to scope which apps are actually reachable. Rationale: Uses the exact affected package coordinate `@hypequery/clickhouse` and the article's fix line (2.0.2 / 2.5.1) so the analyst can version-triage; a file-event hunt reliably surfaces every host with the dependency installed, including transitive/bundled copies TVM scanners often miss for npm packages. goshs launched with vulnerable --no-delete + WebDAV config (CVE-2026-64863) AIReconnaissance High
Hunts endpoint process-creation events where the goshs file server is started with both --no-delete and WebDAV enabled — the exact configuration in which the MOVE verb silently bypasses the delete guard (CVE-2026-64863). Surfaces vulnerable running instances before an attacker abuses MOVE to destroy data. Rationale: Anchored on the exact vulnerable invocation from the PoC (`goshs -d webroot ... --webdav --webdav-port 18081 --no-delete`). The --no-delete + webdav combination is the precondition for the bypass, making this a low-FP asset-hygiene alert. Cross-checked against GitLab GLAD, NVD, and Kali's goshs tool page confirming flag names. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/patrickhener/goshs/CVE-2026-64863/ • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-64863 • https://www.kali.org/tools/goshs/
ATT&CKT1046
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized red-team / pentest engagement legitimately running goshs with these flags
  • CTF infrastructure or training labs hosting goshs
  • Security researcher reproducing the CVE in a sandbox
  • Internal file-drop server intentionally run by an admin who has not yet patched to 2.1.4
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("bash.exe","pwsh.exe") and DeviceName has_any ("lab","ctf","pentest"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm the goshs version from the binary/SHA256 and check whether it is <=2.1.3 (vuln) or already 2.1.4+. Verify the listening WebDAV port is reachable from untrusted networks. Step 2 (contain): Stop the goshs process or firewall the WebDAV port; if the server must stay up, remove WebDAV or upgrade to 2.1.4 which moves MOVE into the delete-gated branch. Step 3 (hunt): Pull web/proxy logs for that host and search for MOVE verbs returning 201/204 (see the correlation UCs) to determine if data was already destroyed, and inventory files under the served -d directory for unexpected renames/overwrites.

Client-side WebDAV MOVE with Overwrite:T header (goshs --no-delete bypass exploitation) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts process command lines that issue a WebDAV MOVE request carrying both a Destination and an Overwrite: T header — the exact curl invocation used to weaponise CVE-2026-64863 (`curl -X MOVE -H 'Destination:...' -H 'Overwrite: T'`). This catches the attacker/operator side of the destructive rename-and-clobber. Rationale: Uses the literal header trio from the PoC (`-X MOVE`, `Destination:`, `Overwrite: T`). The co-occurrence of MOVE + Overwrite + Destination on a command line is a near-unique WebDAV-client signature and directly represents Bypass 2 (destroying an existing victim file via RemoveAll). Confirmed against the GLAD/TheHackerWire write-ups. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/patrickhener/goshs/CVE-2026-64863/ • https://www.thehackerwire.com/goshs-webdav-move-allows-file-deletion-and-overwrite-cve-2026-64863/
ATT&CKT1485 T1070.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate DevOps/backup scripts that rename remote WebDAV objects via curl with Overwrite
  • QA automation testing a WebDAV server
  • Admin manually reorganising files on a sanctioned WebDAV share
  • Pentest tooling (cadaver/rclone wrappers) invoked with an explicit MOVE
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("jenkins.exe","agent.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("backup","deploy"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Extract the Destination URL and source path from the captured command line and identify the target goshs host/port; confirm whether the destination file pre-existed (overwrite = destruction). Step 2 (contain): Isolate the initiating host if the operator is not an authorised admin, and block the WebDAV port on the target server. Step 3 (hunt): Search the same user/host for repeated MOVE calls and for prior 403 DELETE attempts against the same paths (see correlation UC), and validate integrity of files in the goshs -d directory.

| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, SHA256

| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName

WebDAV DELETE blocked (403) then MOVE succeeds (2xx) — goshs --no-delete bypass signature AIActions on Objectives High
Correlates a WebDAV DELETE returning 403 followed within a short window by a WebDAV MOVE returning 201/204 from the same source against the same server. This DELETE-denied-then-MOVE-succeeds sequence is the precise runtime fingerprint of exploiting CVE-2026-64863, where the delete guard blocks DELETE but MOVE still destroys the file. Rationale: This encodes the article's control-vs-bypass contrast exactly: DELETE returns 403 ('delete disabled') while MOVE returns 201/204 and still deletes/overwrites. The 403-DELETE-then-2xx-MOVE pair from one source is highly specific to this CVE and rarely occurs in benign WebDAV use. Defender left empty — Defender XDR has no inbound-HTTP-method telemetry for a locally-hosted goshs server; this must be sourced from proxy/WAF web logs (ImWebSession/CommonSecurityLog). Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/patrickhener/goshs/CVE-2026-64863/ • https://cve.threatint.com/CVE/CVE-2026-64863
ATT&CKT1485 T1070.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A WebDAV client that retries a rename after an initial permission error during a legitimate reorganisation
  • Automated sync tools (rclone/Cyberduck) that probe DELETE, get denied, then fall back to MOVE
  • Web-app scanners/DAST tools exercising WebDAV verbs against a test server
  • Load-balancer health checks that emit mixed verbs (rare, usually GET/OPTIONS only)
Suppression filter
| where SrcIpAddr !in ("127.0.0.1","::1") and DstHostname !has "healthcheck"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Resolve DstHostname to the goshs instance and confirm it is running <=2.1.3 with --no-delete + WebDAV; inspect DenyUrl/MoveUrl to see which files were targeted and whether they were backups/archives. Step 2 (contain): Block the source IP at the proxy/WAF, disable the WebDAV port, and upgrade goshs to 2.1.4. Step 3 (hunt): Enumerate all MOVE 201/204 events from that source over the prior 24h to build the full list of destroyed/overwritten files, and restore affected files from backup.
let win = 2m;
let denied = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where HttpMethod =~ "DELETE"
    | where toint(HttpStatusCode) == 403
    | project DenyTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, DenyUrl = Url;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpMethod =~ "MOVE"
| where toint(HttpStatusCode) in (201, 204)
| join kind=inner denied on SrcIpAddr
| where TimeGenerated between (DenyTime .. DenyTime + win)
| project MoveTime = TimeGenerated, DenyTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, DenyTime), SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, DenyUrl, MoveUrl = Url, HttpStatusCode
| order by MoveTime desc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

Bulk WebDAV MOVE (2xx) from single source — mass destruction via goshs bypass AIActions on Objectives Medium
Alerts when a single source issues a burst of successful WebDAV MOVE requests (201/204) against one server in a short window, indicating scripted bulk deletion/overwrite through the CVE-2026-64863 --no-delete bypass rather than an occasional benign rename. Rationale: Targets the impact end-state the advisory warns about ('any WebDAV client can delete or clobber existing files via MOVE'). A high count of MOVE 201/204 from one source in 5 minutes distinguishes scripted mass destruction from the odd legitimate rename. Threshold-based, so no Sigma. Defender/Falcon/CloudWatch empty — the signal lives only in inbound web-server/proxy logs, not EDR or AWS telemetry. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/patrickhener/goshs/CVE-2026-64863/ • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-64863
ATT&CKT1485
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate bulk file reorganisation / migration job over WebDAV
  • Backup rotation scripts that rename many files at once
  • Cyberduck/rclone directory-move operations
  • A CI pipeline republishing an artifact tree via MOVE
Suppression filter
| where SrcIpAddr !in ("10.0.0.0") and DstHostname !has_any ("stage","test")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Review SampleUrls to see whether the moved paths are sensitive (backups, artifacts, /srv/artifacts as in the advisory) and whether the source IP is an expected admin/automation host. Step 2 (contain): Block the source IP, take the WebDAV port offline, and patch goshs to 2.1.4. Step 3 (hunt): Cross-reference with the DELETE-403-then-MOVE correlation UC to confirm intent, reconstruct the full file-destruction list from the MOVE Destination values, and initiate restore-from-backup for affected files.
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where HttpMethod =~ "MOVE"
| where toint(HttpStatusCode) in (201, 204)
| summarize MoveCount = count(), DistinctTargets = dcount(Url), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), SampleUrls = make_set(Url, 10) by SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where MoveCount >= 10   // 10 = bulk-destruction threshold; benign WebDAV renames are sporadic, not bursty
| order by MoveCount desc

goshs launched with exploitable empty-credential SFTP config (CVE-2026-62325) AIExploitation High
Detects a goshs instance started with an empty-username or empty-password basic-auth value (-b ':pass' or -b 'admin:') together with -sftp and WITHOUT -fkf, the exact command-line state that leaves gliderlabs/ssh with NoClientAuth=true and exposes an unauthenticated SFTP file server. This is the precise exploitable configuration described in the advisory, not a generic SFTP-enable event. Rationale: Uses the advisory's exact exploit signature: goshs binary + -sftp + a -b value with an empty username (':pass') or empty password ('admin:') + absence of -fkf, which the write-up states leaves PasswordHandler and PublicKeyHandler nil and NoClientAuth=true. Cross-checked GitLab GLAD and SentinelOne entries for both CVEs. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/patrickhener/goshs/v2/CVE-2026-62325/ • https://www.sentinelone.com/vulnerability-database/cve-2026-40884/ • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/patrickhener/goshs/GHSA-c29w-qq4m-2gcv/
ATT&CKT1190 T1078.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Red-team / pentest operator intentionally standing up a goshs SFTP share during an authorized engagement
  • CTF or lab infrastructure automation launching goshs with placeholder credentials
  • Internal file-transfer tooling that wraps goshs and passes a colon-terminated -b value by mistake
  • Security researcher reproducing the CVE in a sandbox
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("bash","pwsh.exe","powershell.exe") and DeviceName has_any ("lab","ctf","redteam"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the exact -b value and whether -sftp is present and -fkf absent on the flagged host; identify the listening port (default 2121) and whether the host is internet-facing. 2) Contain: kill the goshs process and block the SFTP listener port at the host/perimeter firewall; if internet-exposed, treat any files served as potentially read/written by anyone. 3) Hunt: pivot on inbound connections to the goshs SFTP port from external IPs and on file create/modify/delete events by the goshs process to determine if unauthenticated access already occurred.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName startswith "goshs" or ProcessCommandLine has "goshs"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "-sftp"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)-b\s+['""]?([^\s:'""]+:(['""]|\s|$)|:[^\s'""]+)"
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "-fkf"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has "goshs" or ActingProcessCommandLine has "goshs"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "-sftp"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)-b\s+['""]?([^\s:'""]+:(['""]|\s|$)|:[^\s'""]+)"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine !has "-fkf"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

goshs basic-auth flag with empty username or password (config-audit hunt) AIExploitation Medium
Broader hunting sweep for any goshs process whose -b basic-auth value is malformed with an empty username (:pass) or empty password (user:), regardless of -sftp/-fkf. Surfaces the root-cause misconfiguration (the && bug at sftpserver.go:85) even on HTTP-only instances or before SFTP is enabled, so operators can remediate the credential string. Rationale: Targets the advisory's stated vulnerable input formats -b ':pass' and -b 'admin:' broadly (any colon-anchored empty credential), so it flags the misconfiguration even when SFTP is off or -fkf toggling changes; annotates SftpEnabled/FkfPresent so an analyst can judge exploitability inline. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/patrickhener/goshs/v2/CVE-2026-62325/ • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/patrickhener/goshs/GHSA-c29w-qq4m-2gcv/
ATT&CKT1190 T1078.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized pentest/CTF deployments of goshs with intentionally weak or placeholder -b values
  • goshs used HTTP-only with a deliberately empty password for a low-value internal share
  • Automation scripts templating the -b value and leaving a colon artifact
  • Developers testing goshs auth behavior locally
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("lab","ctf","redteam","pentest"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the full command line and determine whether the empty-credential side is username or password, and whether the instance is HTTP-only or SFTP-enabled and network-reachable. 2) Contain: instruct the owner to supply both a username AND password (or upgrade past the fixed release) and restart; firewall the listener if exposed. 3) Hunt: check the same host and peer hosts for other goshs launches and for inbound access to the served port to gauge whether the weak config was reached externally.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName startswith "goshs" or ProcessCommandLine has "goshs"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(^|\s)-b\s+['""]?([^\s:'""]+:(['""]|\s|$)|:[^\s'""]+)"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| extend SftpEnabled = ProcessCommandLine has "-sftp", FkfPresent = ProcessCommandLine has "-fkf"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SftpEnabled, FkfPresent, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has "goshs" or ActingProcessCommandLine has "goshs"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(^|\s)-b\s+['""]?([^\s:'""]+:(['""]|\s|$)|:[^\s'""]+)"
| extend SftpEnabled = ActingProcessCommandLine has "-sftp", FkfPresent = ActingProcessCommandLine has "-fkf"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SftpEnabled, FkfPresent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Unauthenticated inbound SFTP to goshs followed by remote file operations AIActions on Objectives Medium
Correlates an inbound connection accepted by a goshs process from a public IP with file create/modify/delete/rename events performed by that same goshs process shortly after — the observable ground truth of the CVE-2026-62325 bypass, where a remote party reads/writes/deletes files over SFTP with no authentication. Rationale: Anchors on the advisory's impact statement ('Unauthenticated SFTP file access (read, write, delete, rename)') by tying an inbound public connection accepted by the goshs process (default port 2121) to file create/modify/delete/rename by that same goshs process within 5 minutes — the exploitation footprint, since goshs itself emits no SSH auth log to prove the bypass. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/patrickhener/goshs/v2/CVE-2026-62325/ • https://www.sentinelone.com/vulnerability-database/cve-2026-40884/
ATT&CKT1190 T1021.004 T1133
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate authenticated goshs SFTP use where the operator did configure proper credentials (the connection was authorized)
  • Internal file drops to a goshs share from a jump host with a public-routable but sanctioned IP
  • Backup or sync jobs writing to the goshs directory concurrently with an unrelated inbound connection
  • Vulnerability scanners connecting to port 2121 that coincide with unrelated file activity
Suppression filter
| where RemoteIP !in ("127.0.0.1") and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "-fkf")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the RemoteIP and whether it is external/unexpected, and confirm the host's goshs was launched with an empty-credential -b value (pivot to the process-creation UCs). 2) Contain: kill goshs, block the source IP and the SFTP listener port, and snapshot the served directory to preserve evidence of read/write/delete. 3) Hunt: enumerate all file operations by goshs in the window to scope what was exfiltrated or tampered, and search for the same RemoteIP touching other exposed services.

| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-62325", "CVE-2026-40884")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
